questions.text: If the cost price of an article is Rs. 600 and it is sold for Rs. 720, what is the profit percentage?
questions.solution: Profit is calculated as Selling Price minus Cost Price, which is 720 - 600 = Rs. 120. The profit percentage is (Profit / Cost Price) * 100 = (120 / 600) * 100 = 20%. Options A, C, and D are incorrect as they do not match this calculation.

questions.text: A shopkeeper allows two successive discounts of 20% and 15% on the marked price of an article. What is the single equivalent discount percentage?
questions.solution: Shortcut: For two successive discounts of a% and b%, the single equivalent discount = a + b - (a×b)/100. Here, 20 + 15 - (20×15)/100 = 35 - 3 = 32%. Step-by-step: Let Marked Price = ₹100. After 1st discount (20%), Price = ₹80. After 2nd discount (15% on ₹80), Price = 80 × (85/100) = ₹68. Total Discount = 100 - 68 = ₹32. Discount % = (32/100) × 100 = 32%.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for: "A person who knows many languages."
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use etymology/root words: 'Poly' (Greek: many) + 'glot' (Greek: glotta, tongue/language). Step-by-step: A Linguist is a scholar who studies the structure of language scientifically, not necessarily a speaker of many. A Grammarian specializes in grammar rules. A Bibliophile is a lover of books. Only Polyglot specifically denotes a person who speaks, writes, or reads several languages.

questions.text: On the recommendation of which committee were the Fundamental Duties incorporated into the Indian Constitution through the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Committee Mapping trick: Swaran Singh -> Fundamental Duties; Sarkaria/Punchhi -> Centre-State Relations; Balwant Rai Mehta -> Panchayati Raj (3-tier structure). Worked Solution: The Swaran Singh Committee (1976) recommended the inclusion of Fundamental Duties (Part IVA, Article 51A) to remind citizens of their obligations. The 42nd Amendment implemented this. The Sarkaria (1983) and Punchhi (2007) Commissions dealt with Centre-State relations, while the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee (1957) recommended democratic decentralization.

questions.text: Pipe A can fill a tank in 12 hours and Pipe B can empty the full tank in 18 hours. If both pipes are opened simultaneously, in how many hours will the empty tank be filled?
questions.solution: Shortcut (LCM Method): Take LCM of 12 and 18 = 36 units (Total Capacity). Efficiency of A = 36/12 = +3 units/hr. Efficiency of B = 36/18 = -2 units/hr. Net Efficiency = 3 - 2 = 1 unit/hr. Time = 36/1 = 36 hours. Step-by-step: Part filled by A in 1 hour = 1/12. Part emptied by B in 1 hour = 1/18. Net part filled in 1 hour = 1/12 - 1/18 = (3-2)/36 = 1/36. Time required to fill the tank = 1 / (1/36) = 36 hours.

questions.text: Choose the most appropriate word to complete the sentence: 'The detective was so ___ that he overlooked the crucial clue in his own pocket.' A) vigilant B) oblivious C) meticulous D) suspicious
questions.solution: The sentence describes someone who failed to notice something important due to a lack of attention. 'Oblivious' means unaware or unconscious of what is happening, which fits the context perfectly. 'Vigilant' and 'meticulous' imply careful observation, while 'suspicious' refers to doubt about others' motives.

questions.text: Which Viceroy is associated with the 'Resolution on Local Self-Government' passed in 1882, which laid the foundation for modern municipal governance in India?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Lord Ripon is famously titled the 'Father of Local Self-Government in India' for his 1882 Resolution. Worked Solution: Lord Lytton is known for the Vernacular Press Act (1878); Lord Curzon for the Partition of Bengal (1905) and Universities Act (1904); Lord Dufferin's tenure saw the formation of the Indian National Congress (1885). Lord Ripon's 1882 Resolution advocated for elected non-official majorities in local bodies.

questions.text: A train of length 150 m crosses a telegraph post in 10 seconds. What is the speed of the train in km/h?
questions.solution: The distance covered to cross a post equals the train's length (150 m). Speed = Distance/Time = 150 m / 10 s = 15 m/s. Converting to km/h by multiplying by 18/5 gives 54 km/h. The other options result from incorrect unit conversions or calculation errors.

questions.text: Select the number that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 3, 10, 29, 66, 127, ?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Observe that each term is 2 more than the cube of its position number (n). 1³+2=3, 2³+2=10, 3³+2=29, 4³+2=66, 5³+2=127. For the 6th term: 6³+2 = 216+2 = 218. Step-by-step: Find the first differences: 7, 19, 37, 61. Find the second differences: 12, 18, 24. Find the third differences: 6, 6 (constant). Since the third difference is constant, the series is cubic. Extend the pattern: next 2nd difference = 24+6=30; next 1st difference = 61+30=91; next term = 127+91=218.

questions.text: Select the word that best completes the sentence: 'The sudden _______ of rain caused a major flood in the valley.'
questions.solution: 'Deluge' refers to a heavy, overwhelming flow of water or rain, which fits the context of causing a major flood. 'Drizzle' and 'shower' imply light or moderate rain unlikely to cause such devastation immediately. 'Mist' is a thin cloud of droplets that does not equate to heavy rainfall. Thus, 'deluge' is the only appropriate choice.

questions.text: The 'Right to Education' was included in which Article of the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution: Article 21A, inserted via the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act in 2002, mandates free and compulsory education for children aged 6 to 14. Article 19 deals with freedoms of speech and movement, Article 32 is about writ jurisdiction, and Article 44 pertains to linguistic uniformity.

questions.text: Deficiency of which vitamin causes the disease 'Pellagra', characterized by the '3 Ds' (Dermatitis, Diarrhea, Dementia)?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Vitamin Deficiency Mnemonics: B1 -> Beriberi; B3 -> Pellagra (3 Ds); B12 -> Pernicious Anemia; C -> Scurvy. Worked Solution: Pellagra is caused by a deficiency of Niacin (Vitamin B3) or its precursor tryptophan. The classic symptoms are the '3 Ds': Dermatitis (photosensitive rash), Diarrhea, and Dementia; if untreated, it leads to Death (4th D). Vitamin B1 deficiency causes Beriberi (wet/dry), B12 causes Megaloblastic/Pernicious Anemia, and Vitamin C causes Scurvy (bleeding gums, poor wound healing).

questions.text: In a certain code language, '257' means 'Watch is fast', '193' means 'Time is slow', and '682' means 'Watch runs slow'. Which digit stands for the word 'runs'?
questions.solution: Comparing '257' (Watch is fast) with '682' (Watch runs slow), the common digit is 2, representing 'Watch'. Comparing '193' (Time is slow) with '682' (Watch runs slow), the common digit is 3, representing 'slow'. Therefore, in '682', since 2 is Watch and 3 is slow, digit 6 must represent 'runs'.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'KITE' is written as 'JHSD' and 'BALL' is written as 'AZKK'. How will 'CODE' be written in that code language?
questions.solution: Comparing KITE to JHSD, the pattern is shifting each letter backward by 1 position (K->J, I->H, T->S, E->D). Applying this same -1 shift to CODE results in BNC D. Option A shifts only the first two letters, Option C has a typo and incorrect last letter, and Option D does not follow the consistent pattern.

questions.text: Statements: Some flowers are red. All red things are beautiful. Conclusions: I. Some flowers are beautiful. II. No flower is beautiful.
questions.solution: From the statements, 'Some flowers are red' and 'All red things are beautiful' implies that the intersection of flowers and red things exists, and since all red things are beautiful, those specific flowers must be beautiful. Therefore, Conclusion I ('Some flowers are beautiful') logically follows. Conclusion II contradicts this deduction. Thus, only Conclusion I is correct.
